newsitem.title: USA: Bond dealers to Clinton--Don't repeal 'de minimis'.
newsitem.headline: Bond dealers to Clinton--Don't repeal 'de minimis'.

text.p: Bond dealers urged President Clinton not to seek repeal of the two percent "de minimis" rule on corporate holdings of tax-exempt bonds when Congress returns in 1997.
Bond Market Trade Association (BMTA), formerly the Public Securities Association, added that if the White House seek repeal, it should delay the effective date to avoid roiling the municipal market.

BMTA Executive Vice President Micah Green made the requests in a two-page letter to Clinton, whose proposals for de minimis repeal in December 1995 and throughout 1996 triggered a major slip in short-term muni prices.
Currently, Internal Revenue Service does not monitor whether a corporation has borrowed to purchase tax-exempt bonds as long as those holdings total no more than two percent.

Clinton sought to wipe out the safe harbor in his fiscal year 1997 budget by proposing that corporations reduce the interest deductin they take on their debt by an amount equal to their holdings in tax-exempt bonds.
The proposal, which would cover all bonds purchased as of Dec 7, 1995, was part of an ongoing Clinton campaign to close corporate tax loopholes.

But the plan died after House Ways and Means Chairman Bill Archer, R-Texas, and Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, R-Del., declared they would not back retroactive application of the provision.

The administration, however, may push the proposal again. A Treasury Dept. official signaled in a September 1996 letter to Modesto, Calif. Mayor Richard Lang that it disagrees with critics of the proposal.

In today's letter, BMTA's Green "strongly" urged Clinton not to reintroduce a de minimis repeal. A proposal "would in reality be nothing more than tax increases on companies, states and localities," he said.
But if the administration does seek repeal, the effective date should be one that would not "shut down market activity."
Green lauded other Clinton efforts, including the president's push for a balanced budget and a recent proposal to help localities fund school infrastructure construction.
Green also said BMTA is helping the Department of Transportion sort out legislative proposals to reauthorize the Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act.
